ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
As shown in Figure A, this is a working schematic diagram of a velocity sensor. P is a fixed small box that emits ultrasonic waves. During operation, P emits a brief ultrasonic pulse toward the object being measured; after the pulse is reflected by the moving object, it is received again by P. Timing starts when P emits the ultrasonic wave, and after a time △t, it emits an ultrasonic pulse again. Figure B is the displacement-time graph of the ultrasonic waves emitted twice. Then which of the following statements is correct?
A. The distance from the object to the small box P is getting closer and closer B. Within the time interval △t between the two emissions of ultrasonic pulses, the displacement passed through by the object is $x_2-x_1$ C. The speed of the ultrasonic wave is $\frac{2x_2}{t_2-\Delta t}$ D. The average velocity of the object during the time t1～t2 is $\frac{x_2-x_1}{t_2-t_1}$

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: According to Figure B, how should the average velocity of the object during the time $t_1\!\sim\!t_2$ be expressed using $x_1$, $x_2$, $t_1$, and $t_2$?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: The average velocity of the object during the time t1～t2 is $\frac{x_2-x_1}{t_2-t_1}$
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the attached image, the experimental situation of Figure A can be seen, namely a schematic of the fixed small box P and the moving cart on a horizontal plane, with a connection to a computer marked beside P; but in the attached image, there is no Figure B displacement-time graph and its labels t_1, t_2, x_1, x_2 that can be directly verified. Then reason: the question stem requires “according to Figure B” and to use x_1, x_2, t_1, t_2 to express the average velocity, so according to the meanings of the symbols in the question, record the positions corresponding to the moments t_1 and t_2 as x_1 and x_2 respectively. The displacement change of the object from t_1 to t_2 is x_2-x_1, and the elapsed time is t_2-t_1. Average velocity equals displacement change divided by time interval, so the average velocity is \(\frac{x_2-x_1}{t_2-t_1}\).
